close_reason: Landed in d64bc4e: pub const MAX_PART_DEPTH=64; private part_to_jmap_inner now carries a depth: usize counter and emits an opaque multipart-typed EmailBodyPart with sub_parts=None at depths >= MAX_PART_DEPTH. Four new tests: shallow round-trip preserves, MAX_PART_DEPTH+4 truncates at exactly MAX_PART_DEPTH levels, 1000-level adversarial input does not panic, truncation marker has multipart type with sub_parts None. README Gotchas adds two entries (adapter bound; upstream parse() still unbounded so consumers must bound message size). PLAN.md adds item 7. Option (a)+(c) per the bead. 20 unit tests + 1 doc-test green; clippy -D warnings clean.
description:
Trigger: an SMTP sender (i.e. anyone on the public internet) delivers an email to a user whose JMAP backend uses jmap-mime, with a multipart/mixed body nested thousands of levels deep. The framing bytes per level are small (`--bnd1\r\nContent-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=\"bnd2\"\r\n\r\n` is ~60 bytes), so a 25 MB message — well within typical SMTP MaxMessageSize — easily exceeds 100k levels.

Path the attacker exercises, all unbounded recursion, all on the parsing worker's stack:

1. `mail_parser` parses the MIME framing (out of scope here; presumably has its own DoS posture).
2. `mime_tree::parse::build_part` (mime-tree-0.3.0/src/parse.rs:131-220) recurses on every `PartType::Multipart` with no depth bound — line 195 calls `build_part` recursively, no `depth` parameter.
3. `jmap_mime::part_to_jmap_inner` (crate-jmap-mime/src/lib.rs:77-106) recurses on every multipart with no depth bound — line 84 `.map(|c| part_to_jmap_inner(c, blob_id_for))` walks children unconditionally.
4. `mime_tree::ParsedPart::find_by_id` (mime-tree-0.3.0/src/part.rs:99) recurses unbounded on lookup, and `message_to_jmap_body` calls it once per textBody/htmlBody/attachments entry (src/lib.rs:138, 145, 152).

Consequence: the parsing worker stack-overflows, the thread aborts (Rust's stack-overflow handler aborts the process by default; the worker thread crashes; the host JMAP process exits or the supervisor restarts it). Either way, the JMAP service becomes unavailable to all users on the affected worker. A single attacker email is enough; re-delivery via auto-reconnect retries the same payload and triggers the same crash, producing a sustained DoS.

Surface attention from this diff: the new `crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs` (lines 116-151, `build_large_deep_multipart`) demonstrates the walker on 5 levels of nesting with the docstring 'exercising the recursive tree walker and the `find_by_id` lookups'. The bench's choice of 5 levels suggests to a contributor that the adapter is happy at that depth — but says nothing about whether the adapter is *bounded* at any depth. A reviewer reading the bench gets no signal that thousand-level nesting is a live DoS vector.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: **availability** of the JMAP message-parsing endpoint, exploitable by any party that can deliver email to the user's mailbox. This is a Section C 'untrusted input at protocol boundary' / 'parsing is total, no panic reachable' / 'no negative test for malformed/oversized input' finding from the crypto-security supplement.

Fix options (maintainer's choice):

  (a) **Defense in jmap-mime adapter.** Add a depth parameter to `part_to_jmap_inner`. If `depth > MAX_DEPTH` (e.g. 64, matching what most production MIME parsers cap at), stop recursing and return an `EmailBodyPart` with `sub_parts = None` (treating the over-deep subtree as an opaque leaf). Document the constant. Add a `#[test]` that builds a 1000-level-deep fixture and asserts the adapter returns a truncated tree without stack-overflow.

  (b) **Push the bound upstream to mime-tree.** File against mime-tree-0.3.0 (or 0.4.x) to add a depth limit in `build_part`. jmap-mime then inherits the bound implicitly. Slower to land; cross-crate coordination.

  (c) **Document the requirement on consumers.** Add a Gotchas entry in crate-jmap-mime/README.md naming the unbounded recursion as a property of the current adapter and flagging that consumers must either (i) bound message size upstream, (ii) bound recursion depth themselves by inspecting `msg.part_index.children` before calling `message_to_jmap_body`, or (iii) tolerate worker crashes on adversarial input. Worst option from a defense-in-depth standpoint but cheapest to ship.

Recommendation: (a) plus (c). The adapter is the right place to enforce its own walker bound; the README note is the right place to set caller expectation for total-message safety even with the bound.

Workspace tracking: this is a crypto-security-supplement finding on the diff covered by JMAP-t307 ('Review: crate-jmap-mime since 9c0d34f'). It is not a duplicate of JMAP-t307.2 (which is about `.expect()` panic-on-malformed input in example/rustdoc — same threat model, different mechanism).
title: Unbounded recursion in part_to_jmap_inner: deeply-nested multipart from SMTP-delivered email stack-overflows the parsing worker
